## Proof

**Yes.** For every real $x$, $f(x)$ is real.

**Key tool — the identity theorem.** If an analytic function on a domain vanishes on a set that has an accumulation point inside the domain, then the function is identically zero.

**Setup.** Since $A\subseteq[0,1]$ is infinite and $[0,1]$ is compact, by the Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem $A$ has an accumulation point $z_0\in[0,1]\subset\mathbb{C}$.

**Construct an auxiliary entire function.** Because $f$ is entire, the function
$$
g(z)\;:=\;\overline{f(\overline{z})}
$$
is also entire: writing $f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n z^n$ (the series converges on all of $\mathbb{C}$), we have
$$
g(z)=\overline{\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n\overline{z}^{\,n}}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\overline{a_n}\,z^n,
$$
which is an entire function of $z$.

**Define the difference.** Let
$$
h(z)\;:=\;f(z)-g(z)\;=\;f(z)-\overline{f(\overline{z})}.
$$
Then $h$ is entire.

**$h$ vanishes on $A$.** For every $a\in A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, we have $\overline{a}=a$, and by hypothesis $f(a)\in\mathbb{R}$, so $\overline{f(a)}=f(a)$. Hence
$$
h(a)=f(a)-\overline{f(\overline{a})}=f(a)-\overline{f(a)}=f(a)-f(a)=0.
$$

**Apply the identity theorem.** $h$ is entire (hence analytic on $\mathbb{C}$), vanishes on the infinite set $A$, and $A$ has an accumulation point $z_0\in\mathbb{C}$. By the identity theorem,
$$
h\equiv 0\quad\text{on }\mathbb{C}.
$$
Therefore
$$
f(z)=\overline{f(\overline{z})}\qquad\text{for all }z\in\mathbb{C}. \tag{$\ast$}
$$

**Conclude for real inputs.** Let $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Then $\overline{x}=x$, so $(\ast)$ gives
$$
f(x)=\overline{f(x)}.
$$
A complex number equal to its own conjugate is real, so $f(x)\in\mathbb{R}$.

Thus $f(\mathbb{R})\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, as claimed. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE

Consider g(z) = f(z) - conjugate stuff... Actually, the standard approach: Consider h(z) = f(z) - \overline{f(\bar z)}. This is analytic (since \overline{f(\bar z)} is analytic when f is entire). For z in A ⊆ R, \bar z = z, and f(z) is real so \overline{f(z)} = f(z), thus h(z) = f(z) - f(z) = 0 for all z in A.
